subject: Renewal healthscore rollup + request for capacity uplift
messages:
From: Jason Kim <jason.kim@blueharbor.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@blueharbor.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 13:17:00 -0500
Subject: Renewal health check & expansion discussion

Hi Olga —

Hope you’re well. Our fiscal review is coming up and the team asked me to get a renewal health summary for our Redwood commitment (current term ends 2027-04-30). We’ve seen a steady increase in peak token usage during promotional events; last quarter we hit about 1.8x expected peak and our SLO-sensitive endpoints showed a few tail latencies.

Two asks: 1) can you share a short health/ROI recap that I can drop into a one-page executive memo, and 2) we’re evaluating a 25% uplift in committed tokens for the next term — want to understand pricing and capacity impact. Procurement copied to keep the timeline visible.

Can we get a brief review + proposed uplift plan on the week of Feb 8?

Thanks,
Jason
Director of AI Platform
BlueHarbor Retail
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Kim <jason.kim@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 14:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Renewal health check & expansion discussion

Hi Jason — thanks for the heads up. I’ve attached a brief usage rollup for Q4 (usage_report_Q4.csv) and outlined initial observations below. I’ll coordinate with Ben and Priyom to put together a one-page executive summary you can use in your memo.

Initial observations (high level):
- Total token spend up 42% QoQ; peak hourly consumption grew ~80% during promo windows.
- Average generation latency on the recommendations endpoint is within SLO (p50 ~85ms), but p99 increased from 420ms to 760ms in late Dec during the promo spike.
- Prefix caching reduced repeat token cost by ~18% on search queries; opportunity for more aggressive KV caching on the recommendations route.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben to propose commercial uplift options (commit + pricing)
2) Priyom to share perf/ops mitigations (autoscale, batching, quantization guidance)
3) Schedule 30m on Feb 9 or 10 for an aligned plan (Olga + Ben + Priyom + Jason + procurement)

Attaching usage_report_Q4.csv for the deck.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Renewals
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Kim <jason.kim@blueharbor.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Renewal health check & expansion discussion

Jason / Olga —

Quick commercial frame from my side: we can support a 25% uplift with two options that balance cost predictability vs. flexibility:
- Option A (Committed uplift): +25% committed tokens, 10% unit discount, guaranteed burst capacity up to 40% above commit for promo windows. Ideal if BlueHarbor wants budget certainty.
- Option B (Flex buffer): +10% commit, with pooled burst credits and a per-token discounted overage rate. Lower commitment, higher marginal cost.

If procurement prefers a short-term pilot before committing, we can do a 90-day trial at the Option B profile and convert with retro credit if you lock in the higher commit.

I’ll draft a term amendment and share a PO template. Olga — want to align on target pricing before I send anything to procurement.

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Kim <jason.kim@blueharbor.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Feb 2027 10:11:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Renewal health check & expansion discussion

Jason — attaching a short ops packet (latency_breakdown_v2.pdf, kv_cache_impact.png) that shows root causes of the p99 spikes and recommended mitigations:
- Enable per-route KV caching for recs endpoint (reduces repeated prefix compute and lowers cost)
- Slightly higher batching thresholds during predictable promo windows (we can keep p50 unchanged and shift some throughput to maximize GPU util).
- If you’re open to model quantization for lower-sensitivity routes, we can propose a mixed fleet that preserves quality for core endpoints but reduces per-token cost on bulk jobs.

Technical caveat: any quantization changes need canarying — I recommend a 2-week canary on 10% of traffic.

I’ll be ready to walk through the slides in the meeting; leaning toward Option A commercially if BlueHarbor values the budget certainty.

—Priyom
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Jason Kim <jason.kim@blueharbor.ai>

Thanks — this is very helpful. Procurement would like to see the draft amendment and a PO template ahead of the Feb 9 meeting. I’m attaching a rough PO (PO_Draft_BlueHarbor.docx) with our internal timeline (we’d like the amendment effective 2027-05-01).

Also can you call out expected annualized unit savings if we pursue mixed fleet + KV caching? My exec will want a 1-page ROI line item.

I’m good for Feb 9 at 10:00am ET.

Best,
Jason
